summary_html: Agency places a child with **relatives or kin caregivers** instead of non-relative foster care. Federal law favors kinship care as least-restrictive, family-preserving placement.

case_law.method: v1.1.0 case-law rebuild: authorities selected per decision point, each opinion retrieved from CourtListener and read; holding and quote taken from the opinion text; independently re-verified before release. Previous keyword-matched Justia listings were removed.

key_cases.holding: The court reversed the denial of a mother's motion to terminate a voluntary guardianship and remanded, holding the parent must first show by a preponderance that the impediments prompting the guardianship are gone, after which the non-parent bears a preponderance burden to overcome the parental presumption, a voluntarily created guardianship itself constituting exceptional circumstances that triggers best-interests review.
key_cases.relevance: Governs kin and third-party caregivers who hold guardianship, requiring them to justify continued custody against the parental presumption.
key_cases.quote: the natural parent must initially prove, by a preponderance of the evidence, that the impediments leading to the creation of the guardianship have been removed.

key_cases.holding: The court reversed the order continuing a guardianship of a child and remanded, because the juvenile court applied a best-interests analysis without first expressly finding the exceptional circumstances required before a child is kept in a non-parent's custody.
key_cases.relevance: Placement of a child with a relative guardian rather than the parent requires the exceptional-circumstances showing, not merely a comparison of homes.
key_cases.quote: The juvenile court's order does not expressly consider or mention exceptional circumstances.

key_cases.holding: The court reversed an award of a stepdaughter's custody to her stepfather and directed that custody be placed with her mother, holding that a court may not award custody to a third party under a best-interests test without first finding exceptional circumstances, which in every case upheld by the court had meant a psychological-parent relationship formed during the third party's actual physical custody.
key_cases.relevance: Governs placement with a stepparent or other non-parent caregiver over the parent's objection, requiring the psychological-parent showing rather than a comparison of homes.
key_cases.quote: Absent exceptional circumstances the natural parent is entitled to custody of the child even though the third party may be able to offer more amenities.

key_cases.holding: The court affirmed an award of reasonable visitation to a stepfather while leaving decisionmaking and primary residential responsibility with the fit biological mother, holding that his psychological-parent relationship was an exceptional circumstance sufficient to justify that lesser intrusion on her constitutional parental rights even though no serious harm or detriment warranted transferring custody to him.
key_cases.relevance: Fixes what a kin or de facto caregiver must establish to keep a legal relationship with the child when the parent objects, and confirms parental fitness is not the test.
key_cases.quote: The existence of a psychological parent relationship can constitute exceptional circumstances justifying the placement of decisionmaking responsibility and primary residential responsibility with a third party.

key_cases.holding: The court affirmed a twelve-month extension of a child's placement in the custody of county social services, holding the findings of continuing deprivation and of reasonable efforts to reunify and to maintain family connections were not clearly erroneous, and that the custodian did not abuse its authority by keeping the child with out-of-state relatives as the permanent plan.
key_cases.relevance: The nearest North Dakota authority on non-ICWA kinship placement: it upholds the agency's placement of the child with a paternal aunt and uncle in another state as the permanency plan and confirms the custodian's authority over placement, subject to the court's power to order the child returned if deprivation ends.
key_cases.quote: The custodian has an obligation and right to determine the nature of care, placement, and treatment of a child considering the child's best interests.

timeline_requirements.consequence_of_miss: The child must be released unless continued shelter care is found required; if no petition is filed within 30 days of protective custody the child must be released from shelter care (N.D. Cent. Code §§ 27-20.3-08(3), 27-20.3-10).

timeline_requirements.starts_from: Receipt of the registered-mail, return-receipt-requested notice by the Indian child's parent, Indian custodian and tribe (15 days where notice goes to the United States secretary of the interior)
timeline_requirements.consequence_of_miss: The first hearing in the proceeding may not be held until the ten days have run; on request of the parent, Indian custodian or tribe the court shall grant a continuance of up to twenty additional days (N.D. Cent. Code § 27-19.1-03(1)).

timeline_requirements.requirement_name: Family case plan filed with juvenile court
timeline_requirements.starts_from: Commitment of the child to the human service zone by the juvenile court (N.D. Cent. Code § 27-20.3-17(1) states only "within sixty days")
timeline_requirements.consequence_of_miss: Not specified in N.D. Cent. Code § 27-20.3-17(1).
